key: And the LORD sent Jerubbaal, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered you out of the hand of your enemies on every side, and ye dwelt in safety.
s: Reproving Israel for asking a king, Samuel recounts God’s past deliverances; Rashi, on 12:11, reads the list as setting three lesser judges beside Moses, Aaron and Samuel, teaching that a lesser leader in his generation is as a great one in his.

evidence.gloss: And Jephthah: here are three of the world’s light ones set with three of its weighty ones, Moses, Aaron and Samuel, to teach that the light one in his generation is as the weighty one in his; every court appointed over the generation must be followed as though it were the mightiest of the mighty.

reason: verse.js ok, ref 1 Samuel 12:11 and at [243,11] match. Plain sense faithful: in chapter 12 Samuel rebukes the people for asking a king (12:12, 12:17) and recounts God’s deliverances through Moses and Aaron (12:6 to 8) and the judges (12:11); no four-word run from the verse. Read the whole chapter 12 packet (Rashi, Radak, Metzudat David; no Midrash Rabbah on 1 Samuel). Rashi on ואת יפתח says the verse sets three light ones (Gideon, Samson, Jephthah, identified in his two preceding lemmas) with three weighty ones, Moses, Aaron and Samuel, to teach that the light one in his generation is as the weighty one in his. The sentence’s paraphrase stays within those words; ‘lesser judges’ is the three named figures, all judges in the book of Judges. Evidence copied verbatim from packet output. entry-check ok.
